comment: MiniDAQ's problem reports (Chapter 14). tools/anomalies.py checks every report and generates known-anomalies.md from the open ones. Dates are when the book found the problem.

reports.title: A number outside the range of double crashed the configuration reader
reports.description: json::out_of_range (406) escaped the reader, which caught only json::parse_error; '6e688' ended the process.

evaluation.rationale: A crash during configure is a lost scan if it happens at the scanner; no wrong value was ever accepted.

reports.title: A sequence jump of 2^31 was counted as two billion lost packets
reports.description: Serial-number arithmetic is undefined for a distance of exactly 2^31; the tracker took the jump as a gap.

evaluation.rationale: Loss counters are how an operator judges a scan's completeness; a false count of two billion lost packets hides the real loss.

resolution.change: A jump beyond the maximum gap is a restart of the numbering (a resynchronization), not a loss.

reports.title: A new run could not open its UDP port while the previous run's detector held it
reports.description: The service created the new run's ports before it released the previous run's, so a second run failed with 'address in use'.

evaluation.rationale: The second scan of a session could not start: a delay, and a repeated injection if the tracer decays meanwhile.

resolution.change: The service releases the previous run's pipeline and ports before it creates new ones.

reports.title: take_all_goods counted a pair twice with per-single windows
reports.description: With a window per single, the pair (a, b) was formed from a's window and again from b's.

evaluation.rationale: Duplicated prompts bias the counts and the image quantitatively without any visible sign.

resolution.change: Only (opener, later single) pairs are resolved in each window.
resolution.verification: CoincidenceSorter tests for SRS-SRT-002, SRS-SRT-003 and SRS-SRT-009

reports.title: SOUP: nlohmann/json 3.11.3 parses an integer as a float if the C library sets errno during a successful conversion
reports.description: Fixed upstream in 3.12.0 (#4506): 3.11.3 treats any nonzero errno after strtoull or strtoll as a failed integer conversion, 3.12.0 only ERANGE. The Chapter 14 review assumed that an errno left by poll() could trigger it; reading the lexer in Chapter 16 showed that errno is reset immediately before the conversion, so only a C library that sets errno on success can trigger it, which POSIX forbids.

evaluation.rationale: The configuration reader requires integers, so such a value would be rejected with a config_error and no wrong setting accepted; with a POSIX C library the defect cannot occur.

resolution.verification: All CI presets, fuzz_config and fuzz_protocol smoke runs, docs.soup

reports.title: A port fault is noticed up to 20 ms late
reports.description: The service's monitor polls the ports every 20 ms, so a run continues for up to 20 ms after a detector or sink fault.

evaluation.rationale: Data acquired in those 20 ms after a fault is part of a run that ends in a fault anyway; the fault is reported and the run is not used. No data is presented as complete.

reports.decision: Release with it. Reviewed against the risk file for release 0.3.0: a faulted run is incomplete in its integrity verdict whatever the delay (assess_integrity, RC-01), and H-05 covers the interrupted scan; 20 ms more data in a run that ends in a fault changes neither sequence of events nor harm, so no hazard needs a faster reaction. Chapter 15 was to decide this and did not; the release review did.

reports.title: The sorter holds its last 104 ns of singles until more data arrives
reports.description: A single can only be judged when a later single shows that its window is closed. A source that falls silent leaves up to the window plus the delay of singles in the sorter until the end of the run.

evaluation.rationale: The singles are processed at the end of the run, so no coincidence is lost; only their latency grows while the source is silent.

reports.decision: Release with it; time markers from the readout would flush the sorter (Chapter 23).

reports.title: The control API has no authentication or encryption
reports.description: Any local process that can connect to 127.0.0.1:7700 can configure, start and stop acquisitions.

evaluation.rationale: A local attacker or a misdirected script can stop a scan or change its settings; the audit trail records it but does not prevent it.

reports.decision: Do not release for use beyond a test bench before Chapter 17's controls are in place.

resolution.change: Token authentication with observer and operator roles, TLS 1.3, secure defaults and API 2.0 (CR-0004, ADR 0014); hazard H-08 closed.
resolution.verification: ControlServer.AnIntruderCannotStopARunningScan, ControlServer.TheTokenNeverCrossesTheNetworkInClear and the other tests of SRS-SEC-001 to SRS-SEC-009

reports.title: Simulation code is linked into the shipped server
reports.description: The synthetic source and the detector simulator are part of minidaq_core, so minidaq_server contains them and a configuration can select them.

evaluation.rationale: A clinical acquisition configured with a simulated source would produce plausible but invented data. The run record states the source type and metadata carries 'simulated', so the data is identifiable.

reports.decision: Release with it for 0.3.0 (MiniDAQ is a teaching project); a product build excludes the simulator or refuses it outside service mode.

reports.title: Pipeline.DropPolicyCountsEveryLostWord failed on a fast CI runner
reports.description: The test assumed that a debug build's sink is slower than its source, so that the drop policy drops; on a fast runner the sink kept up, nothing dropped, and the test failed.

evaluation.rationale: A defect of the test, not of the pipeline: the drop policy was correct. A test that fails at random teaches people to rerun it, which can hide a real failure; that is the reason for CAPA-0001.

resolution.change: dda7a3e: the sink waits until the source has read everything, so the test no longer depends on relative speeds. Recorded as a problem report in Chapter 16 (internal audit, finding A-4).
resolution.verification: Pipeline.DropPolicyCountsEveryLostWord; the stress run in measurements/ch16/

reports.title: FastSorter.FastEnough failed during a CI run on the shared book machine
reports.description: Exercise 10.4's acceptance test compared the run times of two sorters measured one after the other; a slow spell of the shared virtual machine during one of them changed the ratio.

evaluation.rationale: An exercise test of speed, not a test of MiniDAQ; no requirement was affected. Same cause as MDQ-PR-010.

resolution.change: 5d12d87: the two sorters run interleaved, best of seven, so a slow spell affects both. Recorded as a problem report in Chapter 16 (internal audit, finding A-4).

reports.title: The status gained fields without a new minor version of the control API
reports.description: detector_counters (Chapter 9), sorter (Chapter 10), sink_counters (Chapter 12) and integrity (Chapter 15) were added to the status while every response still said "api": "1.0", against the rule of ADR 0003 that new fields come with a minor version.

evaluation.rationale: The integrity verdict is a risk control (RC-01, RC-05): a client cannot tell whether a status without it comes from an older server or is incomplete. No client misread a status, because the only clients are MiniDAQ's own.

resolution.change: CR-0003: control API 1.1 with the status fields listed in status_fields (ADR 0013).

reports.title: An auth request whose token is not a string ended the control server
reports.found: 2026-10-25, GitHub CI fuzz-smoke (fuzz_protocol) on commit dcb701a, after Chapter 17
reports.description: authenticate() read the token with req.value("token", std::string{}), which throws json::type_error when the key is present with another type. Nothing caught it, so one line such as {"cmd":"auth","token":5} from a client that had not authenticated ended minidaq_server (reproduced: abort, exit status 134).

evaluation.rationale: It interrupts a running scan (H-05) without a token, so for availability it bypasses the control of H-08: a process on the PC, or on the network when the server is bound beyond loopback, could end an acquisition. The files written so far stay readable (H-03). Found before release 0.3.0; no released version has it.

resolution.change: The token is read only when it is a string; any other value is an unknown token. The input is in the fuzz seed corpus. CAPA-0003 for the cause.

reports.title: The pipeline's throughput evidence was stale and its regression gate never ran
reports.found: 2026-10-25, release checks for 0.3.0 on commit 4c3ac87 (tools/perf_gate.py run by hand)
reports.description: The performance budget and the verification of SRS-PERF-020 quoted 86 M words/s for the whole pipeline, measured at tag ch05. Since commit 1b6bcd3 (Chapter 10) the pair stage is the coincidence sorter and the pipeline runs at about 39 M words/s on the reference machine (BM_Pipeline 0.44 of the baseline). The gate that should have reported it, .github/workflows/perf.yml, runs only on a self-hosted runner labelled perf, which does not exist, so it never ran and nothing reported that.

evaluation.rationale: SRS-PERF-020 is still met: 37.9 M words/s is 3.8 times the 10 M singles/s it asks for. A pipeline slower than its input loses singles, and losses are counted and reported (RC-01, H-01), so a slower pipeline cannot lose data silently. The defect is in the evidence, not in the software.

resolution.change: Performance budget version 2 and SRS version 6 with the measurement of release 0.3.0; the BM_Pipeline entries of benchmarks/baseline/book-vm.json replaced; tools/release_checks.sh runs the gate before each release (SDP version 4). CAPA-0004 for the cause.

reports.title: The class B items ctl and server have no automated test
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 18 coverage report per software item (tools/coverage.py)
reports.description: The unit tests run neither program. The server's main() (item server: options, security settings, start-up token, shutdown on a signal) has no profile at all, and an early version of tools/coverage.py left it out of the table. The unit tests reach 6 of the 237 lines of minidaq_ctl and none of its 126 branches: no test starts the client. Its parts are tested where they live (TlsContext, TlsStream, read_secret and the control protocol), but not how the client puts them together: that it verifies the server certificate before it sends the token when --tls-ca is given, refuses an unreadable token file, and reports a server that closes the connection.

evaluation.rationale: The client's certificate check is part of the control of HZ-4 (Chapter 17, CR-0004): a client that sent its token before the check would hand an operator token to an impostor. The check itself is tested (TlsStream.ClientVerifiesTheServer), and the client code that calls it was changed and reviewed under CR-0004, so the gap is in the evidence for the composition, not a known defect.

resolution.change: System tests run minidaq_ctl against minidaq_server in their own processes (Chapter 19): exit status, roles, wait, TLS with the right CA and two impostor servers that must receive no byte, shutdown on a signal, refused options and the configuration given at start-up (SRS-CTL-040 to SRS-CTL-044).
resolution.verification: system.control in all six presets. Coverage with the system tests (measurements/ch19/coverage): ctl 81.9% of lines and 77.0% of branches (from 2.5% and 0%), server 80.4% and 81.1% (from not run); the branches not taken are reviewed in measurements/ch19/README.md.

reports.title: The 0.3.0 release commit failed CI: the release record was in no clause of the design file
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 18 local test run (docs.design_file), then GitHub CI runs 40216164998 and 40216375761
reports.description: The release checks ran on 8821c48, a clean commit before the release commit. The release commit b63ff77 added docs/regulatory/releases/0.3.0.md, the first file in that directory, and no clause of docs/regulatory/qms/design-file.json listed it, so docs.design_file failed in every preset and the document-control job failed on b63ff77 and be79f34. The release was packaged and tagged locally without waiting for CI on the release commit.

evaluation.rationale: No code changed between 8821c48 and be79f34: the release commit adds documents and evidence, and the second commit changes a table in the book. Every software test passed on 8821c48 and on GitHub; the failing tests check the index of documents, not the software.

resolution.change: Commit 897a31e lists docs/regulatory/releases/ as evidence for clause 7.3.8. SDP version 5, section 8: a release is tagged and packaged only after CI on the release commit itself is green.
resolution.verification: tools/design_file.py . --check passes on 897a31e; GitHub CI on 897a31e.

reports.title: Two runs with the same seed wrote different records: singles with equal times split across batches
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 19 system test GoldenExact (two acquisitions with seed 1 through minidaq_server)
reports.description: The sort stage orders each batch by time and then crystal (Chapter 3), so a sorted batch is a function of the batch. Two singles with the same time that fall into two batches keep the order in which they arrived, and the batches are cut by time (max_batch_delay_us), so where they fall changes from run to run. The coincidence sorter then took the earlier-arriving single as the first of the pair, so crystal_a and crystal_b (and the energies) of a pair with dt 0 could be swapped: in the first two runs compared, the records were equal up to number 135,698 of 231,650, a pair with dt 0. Counts, rates and spectra were unchanged. Each unit met its own specification; no unit test or property could see the defect, because it is in how the two units are put together.

evaluation.rationale: Both orders describe the same coincidence: the line of response, the energies and the time are the same, and a time difference of 0 has no sign. An image does not change. What breaks is reproducibility: a regression test against golden data cannot tell this from a real change, and a field problem cannot be replayed exactly.

resolution.change: The coincidence sorter puts singles with equal times in crystal order as they arrive (CoincidenceSorter::insert), so its output is a function of the singles whatever the batches; SRS-SRT-013 (SRS version 8). The reference model of the properties orders ties the same way, the sorter generator makes ties common, and the property TheOrderOfTiesDoesNotMatter permutes them.
resolution.verification: Properties.TheOrderOfTiesDoesNotMatter and TheSorterFindsWhatTheReferenceFinds fail without the change and pass with it; the system tests GoldenExact (same seed, and small batches with short delays) pass in every preset.

reports.title: The readout system test counted a packet both delayed and duplicated as a late packet
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 19, recordings for Exercise 19.1 with 5% of each kind of link damage (minidaq_send seed 8)
reports.description: LinkFaults (used by minidaq_send) can delay and duplicate the same packet: it sends the copy on time and the original late. The late original is then a duplicate (stale), not a packet that came after its gap was given up. The system test test_every_damaged_packet_is_accounted_for took every delayed packet that was not reordered as too late, so with 5% of each damage packets_lost and packets_stale were 2 lower than it expected (in one run of seed 8, 108 and 105 against 110 and 107: the run had 2 such packets). The test passed only because its own run (1% of each, seed 5) had no such packet, and minidaq_send did not report the overlap, so no test could account for it. The server's counters were right.

evaluation.rationale: A defect in a test tool and a test, not in the shipped software: the server's link counters were correct. Its risk was a system test that would have failed on a correct server, or passed on a wrong one, at higher damage rates.

resolution.change: LinkFaultCounts counts delayed_duplicated, minidaq_send reports it ('both delayed and duplicated N'), and the readout system test subtracts it from the late packets. A second system test runs with 5% of each kind of damage and requires at least one such packet.
resolution.verification: system.readout: test_every_damaged_packet_is_accounted_for and test_a_packet_both_delayed_and_duplicated_is_a_duplicate pass in every preset; Exercise 19.1's recordings balance with the corrected identity.

reports.title: Under load, the sequence tracker counted a late copy of a held packet as reordered
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 19 system test test_a_packet_both_delayed_and_duplicated_is_a_duplicate, which failed in 1 run of the coverage report and in 8 of 8 runs with the CPUs loaded
reports.description: SequenceTracker::offer counted a packet as reordered whenever it arrived after a higher sequence number, before it checked whether the packet was a copy of one already held. A packet that the link both delayed and duplicated, whose on-time copy was still held behind an earlier gap, was then counted in packets_reordered and in packets_stale. packets_reordered is documented as 'arrived after a higher sequence number, and was still used'. With the server reading in larger batches under load, packets are held longer and the case becomes common: in the failing runs packets_reordered was one or two too high, and the accounting identity of the readout system test failed by the same amount. Delivery, the loss count and the stale count were right.

evaluation.rationale: packets_reordered is a diagnostic counter: it does not enter the integrity verdict, and no data was lost, duplicated or delivered out of order. A wrong diagnostic misleads the investigation of a link problem, so it is fixed.

resolution.change: The tracker counts a packet as reordered only when it is delivered or held, not when it is dropped as stale.
resolution.verification: SequenceTracker.ALateCopyOfAHeldPacketIsNotReordered fails without the change and passes with it; system.readout passed 8 of 8 runs with the CPUs loaded (it failed 8 of 8 before).

reports.title: The readout system tests depended on a receive buffer the CI runners do not have
reports.found: 2026-10-25, GitHub Actions runs of 6919df2 and c3152c7: system.readout failed in the presets debug and tsan and passed in the other four and on the reference machine
reports.description: Two readout system tests send their stream as fast as possible (minidaq_send --speed 0). On the reference machine net.core.rmem_max is 4 MiB, the server is granted a 4 MiB receive buffer and the burst fits. GitHub's ubuntu-24.04 runners keep Ubuntu's default of 212,992 B: the kernel dropped datagrams of the burst before the slower debug and tsan builds read them, the server counted them as lost, and the tests waited 30 s for datagrams that never came. The tests measured the machine. CI ran ctest without --output-on-failure, so its log named the failing test but not the reason; the failure was reproduced by setting rmem_max to the default on the reference machine. The receive buffer is part of the installation (ADR 0009), but the system test plan did not state it as part of the test environment.

evaluation.rationale: A defect of the test environment and its specification, not of MiniDAQ: the server granted what the kernel allowed, reported the small buffer in its detector description, and counted every dropped datagram as lost, as SRS-RDO requires.

resolution.change: The readout tests check the granted receive buffer before they send and fail at once, naming net.core.rmem_max, if it is below 4 MiB; CI sets rmem_max to 4 MiB as the acquisition PC is installed and runs ctest with --output-on-failure; the system test plan states the setting in its environment.
resolution.verification: With rmem_max at 212,992 B the tests fail immediately with that message (4 of 4 runs); with 4 MiB they pass; the GitHub Actions run of the correcting commit passes in all six presets.
